summary_html: Agency places a child with **relatives or kin caregivers** instead of non-relative foster care. Federal law favors kinship care as least-restrictive, family-preserving placement.
authority_html:
- **Fostering Connections to Success and Increasing Adoptions Act (FCSIAA 2008)** — kinship-care incentives  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — reimbursement for approved kin placements

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed, holding that an award of permanent legal custody under 42 Pa.C.S. § 6351(a)(2.1) does not terminate parental rights or strip the trial court of jurisdiction to entertain a parent's later petition for primary custody.
key_cases.relevance: Defines subsidized permanent legal custody, the principal Pennsylvania vehicle for kinship permanency with a relative caregiver.
key_cases.quote: Clearly, our legislature did not exclude from parents the right to petition to modify a custody order entered in a dependency proceeding.

key_cases.holding: Affirming the Superior Court, the court held that grandparents must be permitted to intervene in the adoption proceedings for their grandchildren, and that an agency's refusal to consent does not control because the court may dispense with an unreasonably withheld agency consent.
key_cases.relevance: Foundational Pennsylvania authority that relatives may not be excluded from consideration as caregivers or adoptive resources.
key_cases.quote: A child's interests are best served when all those who demonstrate an interest in his or her welfare are allowed to be heard.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed, holding that 'placement care and responsibility' under the Juvenile Act includes any court-ordered agency supervision of a dependent child, not only cases where the agency holds legal and physical custody, so the youth qualified as having been in placement.
key_cases.relevance: A court-ordered kinship placement with a relative counts as agency placement even without transfer of legal custody.
key_cases.quote: "placement care and responsibility" includes any court-ordered supervision of a dependent child by an agency, not just circumstances where an agency is granted legal and physical custody of a child

key_cases.holding: The court set aside the termination of an Indian mother's parental rights and ordered the child returned, holding that 25 U.S.C. § 1913(b) of the Indian Child Welfare Act allowed her to withdraw her consent to the foster placement at any time.
key_cases.relevance: Shows how ICWA constrains an agency's placement choices for an Indian child.
key_cases.quote: appellant had the right and ability to withdraw her consent to the placement and to effect an immediate return of the child

state_agency.name: Pennsylvania Department of Human Services, Office of Children, Youth, and Families

common_failures: Failure to consider less restrictive alternatives

timeline_requirements.deadline: 72 hours for an informal hearing; no more than 24 hours in protective custody without a court order
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Protective custody may not be maintained beyond 72 hours without an informal hearing under 42 Pa.C.S. § 6332; if custody is continued the county agency must file a dependency petition within 48 hours (23 Pa.C.S. § 6315(d))

parent_rights_at_moment: Right to know where child is going
Right to an informal hearing within 72 hours of protective custody; a child may not be held in protective custody more than 24 hours without a court order (23 Pa.C.S. § 6315(b), (d))
